expectations.name: s4_warns
expectations.detail: event:guard_warn not observed within 155s after relay_edge (seq 1) [BLOCKED: context_valid is never set true by safety_core_build_input() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/safety_core.c) -- S4's `state->s4_warn = in->relay_commanded_continuously && !in->any_current_present` assignment lives inside safety_guards.c's context_valid-gated else-branch and is force-reset to false while context_valid is false, so this cannot warn against present-day SaftyFW regardless of what the fixture does.]

blocked_on.reason: context_valid is never set true by safety_core_build_input() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/safety_core.c) -- S4's `state->s4_warn = in->relay_commanded_continuously && !in->any_current_present` assignment lives inside safety_guards.c's context_valid-gated else-branch and is force-reset to false while context_valid is false, so this cannot warn against present-day SaftyFW regardless of what the fixture does.
blocked_on.phase: Phase 7 (link_task) is built and already publishes this context -- link_task_publish_context()/ link_task_get_context_snapshot() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/ link_task.c) parse and cache every SAFETY_CMD_PUSH_CONTEXT (0x07) frame today. The real gap is one layer up: safety_core.c's safety_core_build_input() never calls link_task_get_context_snapshot() at all (see its own TODO at safety_core.c:208-210), so context_valid stays at its zero-init false regardless of what the ESP sends. A wiring gap in an already-built producer/consumer pair, not a missing Phase 7 deliverable.

expectations.name: s4_never_trips
expectations.detail: dut:K4_open never observed before the boundary [blocked_on annotation is STALE: this expectation now passes -- the DUT appears to have gained the capability the annotation assumed it lacked; consider removing blocked_on from the scenario]

blocked_on.reason: This forbid clause is currently satisfied for the wrong reason: K4 starts de-energized (open) at boot and stays that way, because relay_owner_command_energize() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/relay_owner.c) is fully built but called by nothing in the current source tree -- so K4_open is already true at sim-time 0, before any guard (or lack of one) has had a chance to say anything, not because S4's own correct 'never trips' design held up under test.
blocked_on.phase: Phase 7 (link_task) -- link_task exists and already decodes several ESP->Pico commands (PUSH_CONTEXT, CLEAR_TRIP, SET_CONFIG, ROLLBACK, ANNOUNCE_REBOOT...), but not this one. KilnFW already sends SAFETY_CMD_REQUEST_ENABLE (0x02) over the link (safety_link_request_enable(), App/drivers/ uart_bridge.c), yet SaftyFW's link_task.c has no LINK_FRAME_REQUEST_ENABLE_CMD case at all (confirmed against link_frame.h's command list), so relay_owner_command_energize() is never called from anywhere. A genuinely missing decoder, not a wiring omission on an existing pair like context_valid's gap above -- see ROADMAP.md M4's matching finding.
